subject: Nexus pilot: EU-only hosting confirmation, KMS custody, and SIG/CAIQ attachments
messages:
From: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@nexushealth.com>
To: marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@nexushealth.com
Date: 2026-10-04T09:12:00Z
Subject: Pilot hosting confirmation + SIG/CAIQ items

Hi Marissa —

Thanks again for the demo last week. We're moving Nexus Health to a small pilot and need to confirm a few items before procurement can sign off:

1) EU-only hosting: Can you confirm all inference, logging, and backup storage for our pilot will remain in EU regions (no cross-border backups or analytics exports)?
2) KMS model: We need clarity on who holds the customer-managed key (BYOK) vs Redwood-managed key options. Is HSM-backed KMS supported for Dedicated/Private?
3) Private connectivity: We prefer a VPC peering or PrivateLink arrangement for the pilot. What evidence can you provide for the network boundary and egress controls?
4) SIG/CAIQ: Attached is our SIG spreadsheet. Please populate the control-level answers and attach supporting artifacts where applicable. SOC2 references are fine.

Can we get a documented statement for the EU-only commitment and a short keystore flow diagram for our security review? Procurement has a hard deadline of 10/12 for the pilot PO.

Thanks — happy to hop on a 30m call if helpful.

Elena Rossi
Security Engineer, Nexus Health
elena.rossi@nexushealth.com
+44 20 7946 0123

Attachments: Nexus_SIG_Questions_2026.xlsx
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@nexushealth.com>
Cc: procurement@nexushealth.com, irene.choi@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-04T11:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Pilot hosting confirmation + SIG/CAIQ items

Hi Elena —

Thanks for the clear list. We can support an EU-only pilot; I want to get our technical evidence bundled before sending formal language. Looping in Irene from infrastructure and Karthik from compliance so we can deliver the SIG answers and a concise keystore diagram.

Proposed next steps:
- Irene to confirm KMS/HSM options and provide a keystore flow diagram (by EOD 10/05).
- Karthik to start populating SIG/CAIQ rows with control references and attach SOC2 mapping (by 10/06).
- We will draft a one-page EU-Only Commitment Letter and a technical runbook for PrivateLink/VPC peer (by 10/07) for your procurement.

If that timeline works, we can also schedule a 30-minute bridge Tuesday (10/06) to walk security + procurement through the artifacts.

Marissa
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

Attachment: provisional-runbook-vpc-peering.pdf (draft)
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@nexushealth.com>
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-05T08:22:00Z
Subject: Re: Pilot hosting confirmation + SIG/CAIQ items

Elena / team —

Technical summary below; I kept it high level for procurement and flagged where we will provide artifacts. Happy to expand on any item on the call.

EU-only hosting
- All inference compute, persistent model shards, KV caches, request logs, and backups for the pilot will be constrained to EU regions (Frankfurt and Amsterdam nodes). We will not replicate logs or metrics to other regions as part of the pilot. (Artifact: region-node inventory snapshot)

KMS and key custody
- Two supported approaches: (1) Redwood-managed KMS (Redwood holds keys in our KMS; encrypted at rest), (2) Customer-managed KMS (BYOK) with HSM-protected keys. For pilots requiring stronger custody, we recommend BYOK via customer-managed KMS in the customer's cloud account; Redwood supports external KMS key wrapping for Dedicated/Private.
- When BYOK is used, keys never transit Redwood control plane in plaintext; only wrapped key material is referenced by our runtime. (Artifact: keystore-flow-diagram.png)

Private connectivity and egress controls
- PrivateLink (preferred) or VPC peering available for pilot. Egress is restricted via route tables and we provide flow logs; we can present a network boundary diagram and transient port list. (Artifact: provisional-runbook-vpc-peering.pdf)

SIG/CAIQ and SOC2 evidence
- Karthik will map SIG questions to SOC2 control IDs and attach redacted SOC2 appendix where applicable. For items requiring architecture diagrams or runbooks we will attach the artifacts.

Open items we will include in the packet
- Signed EU-only statement (one-page commitment letter)
- Region inventory snapshot (node IDs + AZs)
- Keystore flow diagram (HSM/BYOK path)
- Network runbook for PrivateLink/VPC peering and sample route table
- Populated SIG spreadsheet with control mappings and SOC2 references

I can be on the 30m bridge on 10/06 at 09:00 BST if that works — send a calendar invite.

Irene Choi
Principal Infra Security, Redwood Inference
irene.choi@redwood.ai

Attachments included: keystore-flow-diagram.png
From: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@nexushealth.com>
To: marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@nexushealth.com
Date: 2026-10-06T10:15:00Z
Subject: Re: Pilot hosting confirmation + SIG/CAIQ items

Marissa / Irene —

Thanks — that level of detail is perfect. Procurement confirmed they need both the EU-Only Commitment Letter (scannable PDF suitable for DocuSign) and a short technical annex describing the keystore custody model. Can you confirm the Commitment Letter will include:

- Explicit statement that production data, backups, and logs for the Nexus pilot will remain within EU-only infrastructure for the duration of the pilot
- The fallback behavior if one EU node is unavailable (i.e., we want to confirm there is no automatic cross-border failover)

Procurement will attach the populated SIG to the PO package; they need the artifacts by 10/12 EOD. If you can provide the DocuSign-ready letter and keystore annex by 10/07 close of business that would keep us on track. Also scheduling the 10/06 09:00 BST bridge now — invite sent.

Best,
Elena

Marissa
